A mutant changes code the mapped test reaches: the item's inputs or scenario, in the single mapped case or file actually run, must pass through the changed line. Before scoring a mutant whose mapped test stayed green, check that the test reaches the mutated line by reading the test and the code path; when that is unclear (mocks, shell or jq pipelines, generated code), put a marker such as `echo reached >&2` on that line, run the same test, look for the marker in its output, and restore the line before making any scored mutant: the marker is a probe and is never part of a scored mutant. A mutant on a line the mapped test never reaches, for example one that only another item's test exercises, says nothing about this item's test: it is a wrong target. Restore it like any other mutant (confirm `git status --porcelain` prints exactly the baseline); it is not scored and is not counted in killed + survived + invalid. Choose one other mutant for the same item on code the test does reach and score that one; at most one re-aim per item, and the re-aimed mutant is the one scored for the item, which is the only exception to one mutant per item. Record each wrong target in `## For the card` as one plain line: file, line, why the test never reaches it, and the replacement. When no change to code the test reaches breaks the item's behavior, the test does not depend on that behavior, so the item is a survivor.
